_meta.note: The second history of shtetl, branch v2: foundations and houses (containers and systems alike) as actors in one C daemon over ZFS. A foundation is one dataset in zlake whose builds are snapshots, beamed to zrun; when a version reaches zrun each house on that foundation rolls onto it: stop, final save, replay into a new version named for the foundation snapshot, swap, start. A failed roll stalls that one object; copies converge to their owner's; old versions are pruned by count once the beam is consistent. The plan is implementation-plan.md beside this file, the author's words its section 18; open-questions.md holds what waits on the author. Paths are relative to the shtetl repository root. Drive this file with tools/tracker.py (its default file). STATE 2026-10-20: every question ruled (plan 18), none open; P1, P2, P5, P6 tested on the box, P3 and P4 wait on a VM; M1 and M2 tested (box run 3, 73 of 73); next M3, m3-builder.
_meta.first_history: branch main (4c0f2c7): its docs/planning.md rulings and probe results are evidence; its code is not carried except the configuration language (plan section 12)
_meta.terminology: house = a container or a system; version = one dataset of a house, cloned from one foundation version; active = the version a house runs from, its newest complete one and the only one mounted; roll = a foundation's next build, or a house's move onto the next version of its foundation; swap = the one act that makes a house's new version active; stall = a roll that failed, the object rolling no more until a person restarts it; shake = merge a recipe's layers into the shaken recipe, injected read-only into what it built; remote = a named place shtetl reaches, a git repository or the lake; beam = a dataset's copy converging to its owner's; owner = the space where a dataset is written.

milestones.M2: shake: the language carried and trimmed, the remotes; a shaken recipe made and injected
milestones.M3: foundations: a real build in zlake on the box, a stall and a restart, pkg, the builder
milestones.M4: beam and prune: both directions, resume after a cut, the counts, pruning that waits for the beam
milestones.M5: containers: create, save, pkg, the roll on a foundation's arrival, the swap, a stall, freeze; a real jail rolled across two foundation versions on the box
milestones.M6: systems: outer space, boot environments, a roll through a reboot, on a VM
milestones.M7: status and syslog, the notifier's interface, the clock

m1-daemon.description: The daemon and the command (plan 9, 10). `shtetl daemon` runs the loop in the foreground and logs to syslog; etc/rc.d/shtetl starts it under daemon(8). It takes an flock on /var/run/shtetl.pid first (a second daemon says it is already running and exits), then replaces any socket left at /var/run/shtetl.sock, mode 0600, so only root reaches it. One kqueue: the socket (EVFILT_READ), each connection (EVFILT_READ, and EVFILT_WRITE while a reply waits on a slow reader), SIGTERM and SIGINT (EVFILT_SIGNAL: the socket removed, exit 0). The wire is framed records over a stream socket, never text to parse: the command sends its arguments as one record; the daemon answers with records of standard output, standard error and the exit status, and the command copies each to its own descriptor and exits with that status. Every other verb is decided by the daemon; an unknown verb is refused with the usage. PROPOSALs: the paths; the command prints, the daemon never writes to a person's terminal (an attended roll passes descriptors in m5-queue). Matrix family D: a daemon forked over the fake ZFS on a listening socket made before the fork. Verify: make check; on the box, the rc script starts and stops it.

m1-foundation-start.description: The first actor (plan 6, 9): one foundation actor for each filesystem under <lake>/foundations, started with the daemon. Starting, it puts the foundation where an idle one is: every dataset of its tree rolled back to its newest snapshot (a no-op when nothing was written), a dataset with no snapshot destroyed (what a crashed first build leaves), the head unmounted. So a crash part way is not a failure and leaves no stall. shtetl:stall on the head makes it stalled, showing the property's text. `shtetl status` prints one line per actor: its kind, its name, idle or stalled, and its newest version or the stall. Matrix family A (actor starts): fresh, written since the newest, no snapshot at all, a child with none, mounted, stalled. Verify: make check; the box run of tests/box/run.sh starts a daemon on md pools after a written head and reads status.

m2-remotes.description: The remotes (plan 4, ruled): shtetl.conf at zconfig's top names the FreeBSD src remote, the patch repositories and the recipe repositories. Each recipe repository is a directory of zconfig of its own, named for its remote; a recipe is found by its name across them, and one name in two is refused as a redefinition is. shtetl clones a recipe repository missing from zconfig and never updates one, so a recipe changes only when the person changes it (ruled 2026-10-20); src and patches are fetched by each foundation roll (m3-src). The lake remote is out of scope (ruled 2026-10-20): it is not read. Verify: make check over scratch trees and local git repositories.

m2-shake.description: Shaking (plan 5): a recipe's layers merged into one UCL document whose every value stands merged, parsed again into the same tree it was made from (a round trip is a cell). A house's recipe stacks on the shaken foundation.conf its foundation version carries: ver constraints both hold, pkg lists join, command pieces the foundation ran are not run again. Injection writes /var/db/shtetl/foundation.conf or house.conf into a tree, mode 0444 and schg, opening every path component beneath the tree's root without following a link (O_RESOLVE_BENEATH on FreeBSD), because a replayed save can hold a link there. The host reads a house's file only from its version's create or update snapshot (.zfs/snapshot), the same way. `shtetl show RECIPE` prints a recipe shaken. Verify: make check; the schg and the beneath-open on the box (tests/box/run.sh).
m2-shake.provides: The shaken recipe: one UCL document, made from a recipe's layers, a house's stacked on its foundation version's; written into a tree read-only and schg, and read back from a snapshot only.

m3-builder.description: The actor's queue and its children (plan 9, 10). An actor takes one message at a time; a message arriving while it works waits in its queue. A step that takes long runs as a child in a process group of its own, watched with EVFILT_PROC, its output to syslog line by line, and the actor answers messages while it waits, its state naming the step. SIGTERM to the daemon ends every child's group before the daemon exits, and each actor starting again finds its step undone or redoes it from ZFS. The builder: one turn at a time across foundation actors, in the order asked, nothing polled. Verify: make check with children that are sh -c scripts; kill tests at each state.
m3-builder.provides: Actors that take messages one at a time and run long steps as watched children; one builder handing out turns.
m3-builder.note: 2026-10-20: built; J1-J12, T1-T3 on the mac (sh -c children), two mutations caught, no leaks, gate, xcheck. No per-actor message queue (what waits is read from ZFS; a busy actor refuses); the daemon's loop integration and SIGTERM stopping jobs come with m3-roll. Owed: make check-freebsd on the box (check_job on FreeBSD kqueue). Worklog issue-docs/m3-builder.md.

m3-src.description: Roll steps 1 and 2 (plan 6), and a recipe repository remotes.recipes names that is missing from zconfig cloned into its directory (never updated, ruled 2026-10-20; from m2-remotes, since a clone is a child): zbuild's checkout fetched from the src remote and reset hard and cleaned to the head of the recipe's src_branch; then the patches, from their remotes in recipe order, each repository's *.patch in natural order, applied with git apply --3way; a clean three-way merge goes on, a conflict is a failure. From main: natural order, the files a patch touches retouched after a reset so make does not take stale objects (main 8b27e68). No pause, no --continue, --skip or --abort, no snapshots of the build root. Each git is a child (m3-builder). Verify: make check with local git repositories; the box build in m3-box.
m3-src.provides: zbuild at the head of a recipe's src_branch with its patches applied, or a failure that leaves zbuild reset.

m3-roll.description: Roll steps 3 to 7 (plan 6) and the stall (7.4). buildworld and buildkernel over the foundation's obj cache (<lake>/foundation-builds/F); into the head, mounted for the roll: delete-old before installworld, the kernel installed into a scratch directory of the obj cache and synced with install -C semantics, distribution, installworld's backups removed (all carried from main as knowledge); pkg, commands-external, commands; foundation.conf injected with the src commit and the patches; snapshot -r F@<ver>-<branch>-<date>-<create|update> with shtetl:kind and shtetl:commit. A first roll creates the foundation's datasets from its recipe. Any failure rolls every dataset back to its newest snapshot (or destroys a first roll's), resets zbuild, sets shtetl:stall (the step and the reason) and logs it. `shtetl roll F` clears a stall and asks the builder for a turn; a roll of a foundation already rolling is refused. Kill tests at each step, the actor started again landing where family A says. Verify: make check with make and git faked as children; the box in m3-box.
m3-roll.provides: A foundation rolls by hand: built, installed, injected and snapshotted, or rolled back and stalled; shtetl roll F restarts a stalled one.

m3-pkg.description: A foundation's package upgrade (plan 6): pkg upgrade in the head, foundation.conf injected again, a snapshot of kind pkg; no src, no build, no commands. A failure rolls back and stalls as any roll. Verify: make check; the box in m3-box.
m3-pkg.provides: shtetl pkg F: a roll of steps 5 to 7 with only pkg upgrade, snapshot kind pkg.

m3-box.description: The box run of M3: tests/box/build.sh on a sparse-file pool kept between runs (its obj cache and src clone, as main's build.sh did, so later runs are incremental), the spaces marked, the daemon started, shtetl roll F by hand: a create roll from releng/15.1, an update roll, a patch that conflicts (stall, the dataset at its newest snapshot, zbuild reset), shtetl roll F after the patch is fixed, shtetl pkg F; the daemon killed during a build and started again (the head rolled back, no stall). The log sent back. Verify: the box log, its first line and its ok/failed line.
m3-box.provides: A real foundation built in zlake on the box by the daemon, a stall from a bad patch and its restart, and a pkg roll.

m4-zfs.description: Layer calls (plan 8.1, probe P1, P5): clone with properties; promote; a snapshot's guid and createtxg; send from a snapshot whole, incremental, or as a clone stream received with -o origin= (lzc_send into lzc_receive_resumable in a forked child, as main's sh_zfs_send forked lzc_send); the receive_resume_token of a filesystem, decoded to an nvlist with zfs_send_resume_token_to_nvlist, and a send resumed from it (lzc_send_resume); a token taken away (receive -A). The fake models a cut stream and its token. Matrix family Z cells for each, on the box and the fake. Verify: make check; tests/box/run.sh.
m4-zfs.provides: The ZFS calls the beam and the houses need: clone, promote, guid, resumable send and receive, a resume token and its abort.

m4-beam.description: The beam (plan 8.1): in origin order, every snapshot a space should hold and lacks is sent, from the newest snapshot of the dataset's history whose guid the receiving space holds, wherever it is there; a dataset new to the receiving space received as a clone of its snapshot of that guid; a foundation's first version a full stream; shtetl:* properties copied after each receive, no send -p. A standing resume token is resumed first; nothing is destroyed on a failure. The actor converges after every snapshot it is told of and on a timer, backs off while a space cannot be reached, and tells the house actors of each foundation version that arrives on zrun. Skeleton rows for run/foundations (canmount=off) and lake/containers, lake/systems. Matrix family B: each shape of history on each side, cut at each stream, a promote before and after. Verify: make check; m4-box.
m4-beam.provides: The beam actor: every dataset's copy converging to its owner's, foundation versions to zrun and house versions to zlake, resuming where a cut left it, telling each foundation version's arrival.
m4-beam.note: 2026-10-20: a lake on another host ruled out of scope; m4-lake-remote removed from the tracker.

m4-prune.description: Pruning (plan 8.2): run.keep house versions on zrun, the active one counted; lake.keep on zlake; nothing leaves a space while the other still lacks it; a version pruned by promoting any clone of it (the newer version's own datasets) and destroying it; a foundation version kept while a house version on the same space is cloned from it, its newest always kept. The house actor prunes zrun after a roll, the beam actor the copies it keeps, the foundation actor a version once its last clone is gone. Matrix family P. Verify: make check; m4-box.
m4-prune.provides: Versions pruned by count once the beam is consistent; a foundation version kept while a house version is cloned from it.

m4-box.description: The box run of M4: the M3 foundation beamed to a run pool, a stream cut part way and resumed by the next convergence, a house version stand-in beamed back, run.keep and lake.keep pruning only once the other side holds what it prunes. Verify: the box log.
m4-box.provides: Beam and prune on real pools: both directions, a cut stream resumed, the counts.

m5-create.description: A house is made (plan 4, 7.1): its first version cloned from the newest foundation version on zrun that the house's ver allows, named <foundation snapshot without its kind>-<house>, shtetl:house on it, every dataset canmount=noauto; a canmount=off placeholder cloned as such; the house's own datasets created; the recipe's packages and command pieces the foundation did not run; house.conf injected; the create snapshot -r, taken last, making it complete; mounted at /containers/<house>. A failure destroys the version. The house actor (one per house, found by shtetl:house on run/containers' children) starts from ZFS: its versions, the newest complete one active, an incomplete one destroyed, the active one mounted if it is not. Skeleton row run/containers mountpoint=/containers. Verify: make check; m5-box.
m5-create.provides: shtetl create H: a container's first version on the newest foundation version its ver allows, complete and active.

m5-jail.description: Stop and start for containers (plan 7.3, probe P2): /etc/jail.conf.d/<house>.conf written whole at each start from the shaken recipe read from the active version's create or update snapshot, never read back; jail -f that file -c, and -r to stop, so jail -r undoes mount.devfs. Main's rulings carried: jexec and pkg -j, digits-only names refused. The daemon starting starts every container's active version. Verify: make check with jail(8) faked as a child; m5-box.
m5-jail.provides: A container stopped and started: its jail made and removed from the block the host writes from its active version's create or update snapshot.

m5-save-pkg.description: A house's own snapshots (plan 7.1): `shtetl save H` snapshots -r the active version, kind save; `shtetl pkg H` runs pkg -j upgrade in the running jail and snapshots it, kind pkg. Each told to the beam. Verify: make check; m5-box.
m5-save-pkg.provides: shtetl save H and shtetl pkg H: snapshots of the active version, kinds save and pkg.

m5-roll.description: The house roll (plan 7.2, 7.3, probes P5, P6): the nine steps in one sequence. The replay runs zfs_rebase as a watched child: the clone form onto the foundation version, the result placed (readonly off, its own path, mounted), then a dataset form a save with -u -b and the pre-apply snapshot named for the previous save, -m always, at most roll.depth saves; each dataset that came from the foundation, parent first; the house's own datasets cloned from the final save. The update snapshot -r last; the swap unmounts the active version, puts its mountpoint back, sets the new one's to /containers/<house>; start. A failure or conflict in steps 3 to 7 aborts any open zfs_rebase run, destroys the new version, starts the active one again, and sets shtetl:stall. A crash: an incomplete version destroyed and the roll run again; a complete one not mounted is a swap left undone, done. Then the prune. A fake rebaser beside the fake ZFS (as main's tests/rbfake.c). Kill tests at every step. Verify: make check; m5-box.
m5-roll.provides: A container rolled onto the next foundation version: stop, final save, replay, additions, house.conf, own data, update snapshot, swap, start; a failure destroys the new version and stalls.

m5-queue.description: The triggers (plan 7.2, 7.4): an arrival told by the beam queues; what waits is read from ZFS (foundation versions on zrun newer than the active version's origin that the house's ver allows), and the house takes the next only when idle and not stalled. `shtetl freeze H` sets shtetl:stall to "frozen" (PROPOSAL); `shtetl roll H` clears any stall and rolls attended: the command passes its terminal's descriptors with its request (SCM_RIGHTS), and at a conflict zfs_rebase --continue -i runs on them, the house down while the person answers; the command stays connected and its signals end the picker, not the roll. An automatic roll never waits and stalls. Verify: make check; m5-box.
m5-queue.provides: Houses roll through every foundation version that arrives, in order; stalls and freeze; shtetl roll H attended, the picker in the person's terminal.

m5-derivations.description: Derivations (plan 7.2 step 3, main's m5-gate): a recipe's derived files, when they conflict in a replay step, are answered keep in the resolution and regenerated by their command in the result (run in a chroot of the run's private mount) before --continue; any other conflict stalls (or, attended, opens the picker). Verify: make check with the fake rebaser; m5-box.
m5-derivations.provides: Derived files answered keep at the replay's conflicts and made again at the gate, as on main.

m5-restore.description: Restore (plan 8.1): a beam the other way, by hand: the house version and its foundation version from zlake to zrun, then made active by the swap, the house stopped and started around it. Whether a restored version counts as the newest complete one is part of the issue: it is, by being made so with a new update snapshot (PROPOSAL). Verify: make check; m5-box.
m5-restore.provides: shtetl restore H VERSION: a kept house version and its foundation version beamed from zlake back to zrun and made active.

m5-box.description: The box run of M5: a container created on the M3 foundation, saved, the foundation rolled and beamed, the container rolling on its arrival by itself; a save that conflicts with the next foundation version stalls it, shtetl roll H after; freeze holds it through an arrival; the daemon killed mid-roll and started again; the time the house was down recorded (plan 16). Verify: the box log.
m5-box.provides: A real jail rolled across two foundation versions on the box, with a conflict stalled, a freeze, and the roll timed.

m6-boot-envs.description: Systems (plan 7.3, probe P3): a system's versions under run/systems, the root mountpoint=/, root and children canmount=noauto; create as for a container with the system's own commands chrooted before its first boot; the swap is zpool set bootfs; the active version is the one bootfs names. Skeleton row run/systems. Needs P3's VM result first. Verify: make check; m6-vm.
m6-boot-envs.provides: A system's versions as boot environments under run/systems, the active one bootfs.

m6-outer-space.description: Stop and start for systems (plan 7.3, ruled 2026-10-15, probe P4): a memory disk made a pool, the current root sent into it, vfs.root.mountfrom pointed at it, reboot -r; the daemon starting there finds itself in outer space and does steps 2 to 8 of the roll for that system only; start is a real reboot, which loads the new kernel; a failed roll reboots into the bootfs it did not change. Needs P4's VM result first. Verify: make check for the decisions; m6-vm.
m6-outer-space.provides: A system rolled through outer space: stopped by reboot -r into a memory-disk root, steps 2 to 8 done there, started by a real reboot.

m6-vm.description: The VM run of M6: a scratch FreeBSD 15.1 VM with root on ZFS, a system created from the M3 foundation and booted, the foundation rolled and beamed, the system rolling through outer space and coming up on its new version; a failing roll coming back up on the old one. Staged across reboots by state read from ZFS, as P3 and P4 are. Verify: the VM log.
m6-vm.provides: A system rolled through a reboot on a VM.

m7-status.description: Status and syslog (plan 7.4, ruled): `shtetl status [NAME]` shows each actor: its state and the step under way, the foundation versions a house has waiting, a stall's step and reason, the beam's lag; every message an actor tells (a version, a snapshot, a stall, an arrival) logged to syslog once. Verify: make check.
m7-status.provides: shtetl status showing every actor's state, step under way, queue and stall; every tell in syslog.

m7-notifier.description: The notifier (plan 7.4, ruled "a pluggable interface", worked out at the very end): an actor told of every stall, handing it to whatever the site plugs in. What a plug-in is (a program run with the stall on its standard input is the recommendation) is asked of the author when this issue starts. Verify: make check.
m7-notifier.provides: The notifier actor and its pluggable interface; its channels left to the author.

m7-clock.description: The clock (plan 2 rule 4, 9): a foundation recipe's schedule key (its form proposed with the issue), read from the shaken recipes; at each due time the clock sends the foundation actor the same roll message `shtetl roll F` sends, with EVFILT_TIMER; a stalled foundation ignores it as it ignores any roll but the person's. No other schedule exists. Verify: make check with the clock's time injected.
m7-clock.provides: Each foundation's schedule, the only schedule: the clock sending the roll message a person could send.
